summary: Mong Hsat Airport (MOG) is a medium-sized domestic airport located in the remote town of Mong Hsat in eastern Shan State, Myanmar, near the Thai border. The airfield has notable historical significance, originally developed as a Royal Air Force base during World War II and later utilized by US Air Force operations. Today it primarily serves regional flights connecting this frontier area to other parts of Myanmar.
faqs:
Q: Are there international flights from Mong Hsat Airport?
A: No, the airport currently handles only domestic flights within Myanmar.

Q: How far is the airport from Mong Hsat town center?
A: The airport is located a short distance from the town, typically a quick drive from the central area.

Q: Which airlines operate from Mong Hsat Airport?
A: Domestic carriers serving the route include Myanmar National Airlines and regional operators connecting to major hubs like Mandalay and Yangon.

Q: Is the airport used for military purposes?
A: The airfield has historical military significance and retains some strategic importance alongside its civilian operations.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Mong Hsat Airport is best done by pre-arranged taxi or hotel transfer, as public transportation options are limited in this remote area. The town center is only a short drive away, so journey times are typically brief. Travelers heading to the Thai border should arrange onward transport in advance, as border crossing logistics require planning.
local_tip: Flights to Mong Hsat are infrequent and often weather-dependent due to the mountainous terrain, so build buffer days into your itinerary and confirm schedules locally before committing to onward travel plans.
